headline: Maritime Logistics and Mainland Parking Procedures
reservation: Overnight camping and RV stays are strictly prohibited on the island to protect the fragile ecosystem. Ferry vehicle space is extremely limited and requires booking months in advance through official ferry operators; foot passengers generally have more flexibility but should check seasonal schedules for the Point Judith and New London routes.

days.title: Victorian Harbors and Historic Beacons
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM from Old Harbor Ferry Terminal

stops.name: Southeast Lighthouse
stops.detail: Visit this 1874 brick marvel perched atop the Mohegan Bluffs for sweeping views of the Atlantic.

stops.name: Mohegan Bluffs
stops.detail: Descend the steep wooden staircase to the secluded beach beneath 150-foot clay cliffs.

days.driving: Local bicycle or moped transfer; walking is recommended within the Old Harbor district.
days.note: Moped rentals require safety briefings and are restricted on certain unpaved island paths.

days.title: Conservation Trails and Great Salt Pond
days.start: Suggested: 8:30 AM from the Greenway Trailhead

stops.name: Clayhead Preserve
stops.detail: Walk the 'Maze' trails for migratory bird sightings and dramatic views of the northern coastline.

stops.name: Great Salt Pond
stops.detail: A hub for kayaking and observing the island's maritime culture away from the main ferry hub.

days.driving: Allow 20 minutes for cycling between the north and south ends of the island.
days.note: Tick prevention is essential when walking through the maritime shrubland and grasses.

days.title: North Light and Quiet Coastal Rhythms
days.start: Suggested: 10 AM from Corn Neck Road

stops.name: North Light
stops.detail: A scenic trek to the northernmost tip where the Atlantic meets the Block Island Sound.

stops.name: Crescent Beach
stops.detail: Enjoy the island's primary stretch of sand, ideal for a final walk before the return ferry.

days.driving: Walking or bicycle travel only; no vehicle parking at the immediate North Light site.
days.note: The walk to North Light is over soft sand and cobble; allow extra time for the 2-mile round trip.

intel.title: Mainland Terminal Lots
intel.text: Use the long-term satellite lots at Point Judith; these areas often require cash payments and fill quickly during summer holiday weekends. Island parking is restricted to residents and short-term visitors in designated Old Harbor zones.

intel.title: Island Connectivity
intel.text: Cell service is generally reliable in Old Harbor but drops significantly on the Greenway trails and the western bluffs. Do not rely on digital maps for navigating the interior conservation lands.

intel.title: Island Resource Limits
intel.text: A single fuel station serves the island near the Great Salt Pond; prices reflect the cost of maritime transport. It is advisable to fuel vehicles on the mainland before boarding the ferry.

intel.title: Ferry Arrival Logic
intel.text: Arrive at the mainland terminal at least 45 minutes prior to departure, especially if you have bicycle or luggage tags to process. The final ferry of the day is a hard cutoff; no alternative transit exists after hours.

intel.title: Private Land Sensitivity
intel.text: Large portions of the island are private or managed conservation land. Always stay on marked Greenway trails to prevent erosion and respect local property boundaries.

plan.arrival: Arrive at Point Judith, RI for ferry boarding; upon arrival at Old Harbor, visit the visitor center before walking to your historic inn or renting bicycles.
plan.vehicle: Bicycles and mopeds are the preferred island transport; bringing a car is expensive and often unnecessary for a short stay.
plan.goldenHour: Southeast Lighthouse offers a dramatic viewpoint for sunrise, while the North Light is a favored spot for sunsets over the water.
